subject: Connexa technical onramp — SDK, auth, routing & local sandbox
messages:
From: Jessica Park <jessica@connexa.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Connexa technical onramp — SDK, auth, routing & local sandbox

Hi Irene / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — we liked the latency profile and the canary fallback story. Per our internal conversation, here are the things we need to validate to get a small internal pilot going: 

- Quickstart SDK run in our dev environment (Python + TypeScript examples)
- Auth options: API keys vs OAuth + how to integrate with our Okta SSO and KMS
- Routing policy: how to route by latency/cost/region (US primary, EU DR)
- Structured output / tool-calling examples (we plan to call a medical rules engine as an external tool)
- Embeddings + reranker guidance for our note-search (250k docs)
- Local sandbox to run end-to-end without sending PHI to hosted endpoints

Can you send a concrete onramp plan with commands we can run locally and an ETA for a 60–90 minute technical deep dive next week? Attaching the initial security questionnaire we filled out — you can see a couple of KMS / audit-log questions we flagged.

Attachments: security-qa.xlsx

Thanks,
Jessica
VP Product, Connexa Health

From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Connexa technical onramp — SDK, auth, routing & local sandbox

Hi Jessica — great to meet you on the call. High-level plan and runnable quickstart below. I attached a short guide (redwood-sdk-quickstart.md) and a tiny sample app (connexa-sample-app.zip) that mirrors the flow you described.

Quick summary (actionable):
1) Local sandbox (no PHI leaves your laptop)
   - Clone the sample app: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/connexa-sample-app.git
   - Python venv approach:
     - python3 -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
     - pip install -r requirements.txt
     - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<local-sandbox-key>  # we will provide time-limited sandbox keys
     - export REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://sandbox.redwood.local  # sample local proxy + model runtime
     - python run_local_demo.py --use-embeddings --rerank
   - TypeScript (Node) quickstart:
     - npm ci && npm run build
     - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=<local-sandbox-key>
     - npx ts-node src/demo.ts --mode sandbox

2) Auth & KMS integration options
   - API keys: fastest for pilot; keys scoped per environment and can be short-lived via the Console.
   - OAuth/OIDC: we support OIDC; you can map Okta groups to roles at the RBAC layer.
   - KMS/HSM: Redwood Private supports customer KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS; for hosted pilot we can create envelope encryption with your KMS (we'll exchange a wrapped key).

3) Routing & cost policy (sample config snippet in redwood-sdk-quickstart.md)
   - route_by: [latency, cost] with fallback to smaller model family during high load
   - region_priority: [us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1]
   - example: {"route_by": "latency", "preferred_tiers": ["dedicated","hosted"]}

4) Structured output & tool calling
   - We recommend using the function-calling API for deterministic tool invocation.
   - Secure tool webhooks: sign requests with a JWT using your Okta OIDC provider; we provide a helper middleware (in sample app) to verify payloads.
   - Example: model returns JSON with fields {"action":"call_rules_engine","input":{...}} — sample handler in src/handlers/tool_runner.py

5) Embeddings + reranker guidance
   - For 250k docs: use batched embedding generation with incremental upsert into your vector DB.
   - Use 1536-d embeddings for initial pilot (balance perf/cost). If you need higher recall, we can test 3072-d variants.
   - Reranker: coarse retrieval (ANN) -> top-K rerank with a short-context cross-encoder. We include an example reranker in the sample app that calls Redwood's rerank endpoint.

Next steps & timeline - I'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive: proposed slots Wed/Thu next week (I added a Doodle in the shared Drive link).
- Aditya will prep a short demo of the routing policy and failover behavior.
- Neha will own the security/KMS Q&A and provide answers to your spreadsheet by EOD Thu.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md, connexa-sample-app.zip

Let me know which slot works and any constraints for your security team.

—
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0104

From: Marcus Lee <marcus@connexa.ai>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jessica Park <jessica@connexa.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connexa technical onramp — SDK, auth, routing & local sandbox

Irene — thanks for the detailed plan. A few quick clarifying questions before the deep dive so we can prepare internal folks: 

1) Embeddings size: you mentioned 1536 vs 3072 dims. Do you have a rough cost per 1M tokens/embeds estimate for each? We want to model monthly cost.
2) Reranker latency: the plan to do ANN -> top-K rerank is clear, but what approximate P50/P90 latency should we expect for a cross-encoder reranker on a 16-core CPU (no GPU) for top-20 candidates?
3) Tool calling security: when the model triggers a call to our rules engine, what auth does Redwood include in the outbound webhook? Can we enforce mutual TLS or signed JWTs?
4) Local sandbox keys: how long do those keys last and can they be rotated programmatically?

Also attaching a short doc with our expected concurrency patterns so you can recommend batching settings.

Cheers,
Marcus
Engineering Manager, Search & Retrieval, Connexa

From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lee <marcus@connexa.ai>, Jessica Park <jessica@connexa.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connexa technical onramp — SDK, auth, routing & local sandbox

Marcus — quick answers inline and a short plan for the deep dive. Forwarding the security spreadsheet answers as a follow-up by EOD.

1) Embeddings cost (approx, hosted API rates)
   - 1536-d: ~$0.45 per 1k embeddings (ballpark for pilot)
   - 3072-d: ~ $0.75 per 1k embeddings
   - We'll run a small sampling job during the deep dive to give a precise estimate against your dataset.

2) Reranker latency (cross-encoder, CPU only)
   - P50: ~60–120ms for top-20 on a 16-core vCPU machine (depends on model size)
   - P90: ~200–450ms; if you need tighter SLOs we recommend a small GPU or quantized CPU runtimes we can benchmark.

3) Tool-calling auth
   - Outbound webhooks can use signed JWTs (we sign with a Redwood service key) and we can also support mTLS for Private deployments.
   - For hosted pilots: signed JWT + timestamp + nonce (replay protection) is typical; we'll include verification middleware in the sample app.

4) Sandbox keys
   - Time-limited (default 24 hours) and programmatically rotatable via the Console API. We can extend per request for your dev squad.

Proposed deep-dive agenda (60 min)
- 0–10m: introductions + success criteria (Jessica)
- 10–25m: live walkthrough of the sample app (Irene + Aditya)
- 25–40m: embeddings + reranker tuning + batching recommendations (Aditya)
- 40–55m: security/KMS & tool-calling auth (Neha)
- 55–60m: next steps and owners

Proposed prep items for Connexa
- A small sample of your notes (anonymized) for onsite benchmarking (optional)
- Expected concurrency document (you mentioned you'll attach this)

Confirmed deliverables after the call
- Sandbox keys for your team
- A set of benchmark numbers for your data profile
- Answers to the security questionnaire (security-qa.xlsx)

Meeting link (pick a slot): https://cal.com/redwood/connexa-tech-deep-dive
Drive prep folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123

Thanks — we'll get Neha's security answers in by EOD Thu as promised. If that works I will send a calendar invite once you confirm a slot.

Best,
Irene
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
